summary: PulseGuard v0.6.36 is a cross-machine correctness pass driven by v0.6.35 testing: it removes false Store/WindowsApps corruption findings, strengthens executable ownership, verifies side-by-side .NET updates correctly, improves OEM/startup classification, and cleans customer-facing maintenance truth labels.

sections.heading: Protected Store/WindowsApps targets no longer become false corruption
sections.detail: A protected WindowsApps or Store launch alias that Windows refuses to open is classified PROTECTED/UNVERIFIABLE unless independent corruption evidence exists. Access denial alone can no longer subtract application-integrity health points.

sections.heading: Installed-app executable ownership is stricter
sections.detail: App Paths now require distinctive app-name tokens and strong ownership evidence before an executable is hashed or structure-tested. Generic words can no longer attach unrelated executables such as GetHelp.exe to another installed program.

sections.heading: .NET side-by-side updates receive architecture-aware verification
sections.detail: Microsoft .NET, ASP.NET Core and Windows Desktop Runtime updates are verified by target shared-runtime evidence plus an exact WinGet recheck. Older side-by-side runtime versions may remain installed without causing a false verification-pending result, and the detected installer architecture is retained as verification evidence.

sections.heading: Temporary WinGet/vendor installer crashes no longer reduce general PC health
sections.detail: Crash events from temporary WinGet/PulseGuard installer paths remain in diagnostic history and application-update review, but are excluded from the active repeated-app instability set and health-score penalty.

sections.heading: ASUS support routing is consistent on uncurated boards
sections.detail: When an ASUS board lacks a curated static rule, PulseGuard still exposes the exact official ASUS board support route and explicitly labels automatic OEM archive discovery as incomplete rather than implying all OEM drivers were proven current.

sections.heading: More common startup entries are classified
sections.detail: Overwolf, Opera/Opera Air/Opera GX user auto-start, U.GG, LG OnScreen Control and Send to OneNote now have researched startup classifications while the existing keep-first safety policy remains intact.

sections.heading: Changes Recorded uses customer-facing completion language
sections.detail: Successful Deep Clean and Privacy maintenance display Completed, successful media-aware volume optimization displays Verified, and application-update batches display Verified or Review according to package-level evidence instead of generic Unverified wording.

sections.heading: Skipped healthy repair lanes finish as completed
sections.detail: A repair lane that intentionally returns SKIPPED because the system is already healthy, no update is needed, or a maintenance cooldown is active no longer leaves the grouped Optimize status looking in-progress. Reboot-required and unresolved warning states remain visible.
